dossier.public_summary: The 0.66-day dip does not come from the target star. Difference imaging places it about 75 arcseconds away on a faint neighbour that only needs a ~1% eclipse. The dip’s long duration and strong 3000 ppm phase-curve signal match a blended eclipsing binary, not a 1.9 Earth-radius planet on the M dwarf.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip 75 arcsec from the target, coincident with a Gaia star at 69.1 arcsec needing only 0.0124 eclipse depth, ruling out a planet on the target
reasons.value: off_target, offset 75.19" +/-13.72" (5.481 sigma), on_star sep 69.1" sigma 2.5

reasons.why: Large out-of-eclipse swing at the 0.656 d period is inconsistent with a planet transit and indicates ellipsoidal/spots from a close eclipsing binary on the neighbour
Duration far too long for the target M dwarf, but fits a binary on a different star, supporting a blended eclipse not on target
reasons.value: 1.826, observed 1.231 h vs central 0.6742 h for TIC rad 0.2629

reasons.why: Target shows ultra-short 0.66 d variability (Teff 3226 K M dwarf) but the dip is 75 arcsec away, the variability is spot modulation on the target uncorrelated with the off-target eclipse
